item.title: Analysing Busy Beaver Machines (Or How to Find Ossified Ocelots)
item.description: arXiv:2611.17742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The busy beaver problem involves working with machines which can produce very large numbers, both for the output of certain Turing machines and for the number of steps taken to execute them. Given that these numbers can involve thousands of digits, it is crucial to have a means of proving properties of the relevant machines which allow manipulation of such large numbers. In this paper we introduce the notion of \textit{shape computations} as a means of isolating key properties that allow efficient execution of the relevant Turing machines based on verifiable properties of state transitions. In particular, this notion allows us to provide an analytical result which demonstrates the quadratic relationship between the size of the output and the number of steps required to generate it. We have also developed an initial implementation of our approach, and we provide empirical evaluation of it on a suite of 240 example machines.
item.dc:creator: James Harland

item.title: Additive cubes are avoidable over $\{0,1,2,3\}$, $\{0,1,4\}$ and $\{0,2,5\}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.17999v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over the alphabet $\{0,1,2,3\}$, thereby solving a long-standing question initiated by Pirillo and Varricchio in 1994. By extending the reduction and spectral machinery of Cassaigne, Currie, Schaeffer, and Shallit (2014), we prove that the search for additive cubes in such morphic images reduces to a finite graph traversal. We exhibit eight explicit morphisms from $\{0,1,3,4\}^*$ to $\{0,1,2,3\}^*$ of length 3 whose images on the Cassaigne \textit{et al.} infinite word contain no additive cubes.
item.dc:creator: Damien Jamet, Matthieu Rosenfeld

item.title: Stochastic Games with Distributional Entropy Objectives
item.description: arXiv:2611.18470v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce \emph{stochastic games with distributional entropy objectives}, two-player zero-sum games whose configurations are probability distributions over the states of a finite arena and whose stage reward is Shannon entropy. Over an infinite discounted horizon, MIN seeks to concentrate the distribution, while MAX seeks to disperse it. Because entropy is nonlinear, it matters whether strategic and transition randomness are averaged before entropy is evaluated or sampled first. We formalise three resulting semantics: averaged-distribution, sampled-profile, and sampled-transition. This semantic choice fundamentally changes the game-theoretic structure. Averaged-distribution games need not be determined, even on a four-state deterministic arena, whereas both sampled semantics are determined and admit optimal stationary randomised strategies. We give contractive Bellman characterisations and convergent finite-horizon approximations for the upper and lower averaged values and the two sampled values. Moreover, even the lower value under averaged-distribution semantics dominates the value under either sampled semantics, while the sampled-profile and sampled-transition values are incomparable in general. For fixed rational discount and positive rational promise gap, the averaged-distribution (upper and lower value) gap problems and both sampled gap problems lie in PSPACE; for a single entropy minimiser, the averaged and sampled-profile problems lie in NP. Finally, under all three semantics, entropy optimisation is NP-hard to approximate within a suitable fixed additive constant, already for deterministic one-player games, where pure memoryless strategies are optimal.
item.dc:creator: Shankaranarayanan Krishna, Durgam Latha, Dion Reji, Ashutosh Trivedi

item.title: An 'Experimental Mathematics' Approach to Stolarsky Interspersions via Automata Theory
item.description: arXiv:2502.03312v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We look at the Stolarsky interspersions (such as the Wythoff array) one more time, this time using tools from automata theory. These tools allow easy verification of many of the published results on these arrays, as well as proofs of new results.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Shallit

item.title: Regular Separability for Bidirected VASS
item.description: arXiv:2611.03313v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The regular separability problem asks, given two languages, whether there exists a regular language that contains one of them and is disjoint from the other. We study regular separability for bidirected VASS. We first show that the problem remains Ackermann-complete when the input consists of two languages recognised by bidrected VASS. To find a subclass of VASS in which the problem has lower complexity we define alphabetically bidirected VASS as ones where bidirectedness is also visible in the input letters. Our main result establishes that regular separability for alphabetically bidirected VASS is EXPSPACE-complete. The key to this result is that, in this setting, regular separability coincides with disjointness. As a first ingredient in this equivalence, we also show that for alphabetically bidirected Z-VASS, regular separability and disjointness are equivalent. Consequently, regular separability for these systems is in polynomial-time. In fact, it is log-space inter-reducible with non-solvability of integer linear Diophantine equation systems. Finally, we observe that the picture changes dramatically in the presence of a zero test, namely, we show that regular separability for alphabetically bidirected one-counter automata is undecidable.
item.dc:creator: {\L}ukasz Orlikowski, Georg Zetzsche

item.title: Some complete $\omega$-powers of a one-counter language in the difference hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2610.16473v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fix a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ having at least two letters, and natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$. We denote by $D_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$ the class of differences of $n$ subsets of the Cantor space $\Sigma^\omega$ in $\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k$, and by $D^-_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$ the class of complements of sets in $D_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$. We prove, for any natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$, the existence of a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ having at least two letters and a finitary language $U_{n,k}$ over $\Sigma$ accepted by a one-counter automaton such that the $\omega$-power $$U_{n,k}^\infty:=\{ w_0w_1\cdots\in\Sigma^\omega\mid\forall i\in\omega ~~w_i\in U_{n,k}\}$$ is $D_{2n-1}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$-complete. We also prove a conditional result for the dual classes $D^-_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$: under the assumption that there exists a finitary language $V_{n,3}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $\omega$-power $V_{n,3}^\infty$ is $D^-_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_3)$-complete, there would also exist, for any integer $k > 3$, a finitary language $V_{n,k}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $\omega$-power $V_{n,k}^\infty$ is $D^-_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$-complete. Finally we add another conditionnal result about Wadge degrees of rational $\mathbf{\Delta}^0_2$ omega powers, which completes the recent results of [FGL26].
item.dc:creator: Jacques Duparc (UNIL), Olivier Finkel (IMJ-PRG), Dominique Lecomte (IMJ-PRG)
